stances.claim: Henry Sy's lifelong arc -- from immigrant shoe-store proprietor in 1940s Carriedo to wealthiest Filipino with a 930-hectare global retail footprint by his death -- illustrates that singular vision and passion, sustained over decades, can transform a national landscape (notably his prescient 1970s vision of Edsa as the metropolitan artery for supermalls).

Sy's most distinctive personal quality was his humble self-effacement -- never flaunting wealth, calling his children 'teammates,' calling Molly 'best friend,' tending SM Foundation 'as passionately as he did his gigantic businesses,' and refusing to speak with CJ during his 11+ Supreme Court years out of respect for judicial independence.
stances.rhetorical_move: humility-as-defining-trait portrait with specific behavioral evidence

stances.claim: Sy's quiet, unobtrusive appearance at CJ's retirement reception -- 'showed up, quietly greeted me and left as unobtrusively as when he came in' -- captures the essence of his character: he gave honor without seeking it, expressed friendship without claiming it.

Hans Sy's private confidence at Tatang's wake -- that the National University 20-campus 100,000-scholar expansion was not yet reached but 'would [be] in a few years' -- is the most consequential legacy commitment in the Sy succession, transforming SM's commercial empire into an educational philanthropy at unprecedented scale.

notable_anecdotes: The grand deal in 1940s Carriedo: CJ as poor newsboy haggling from Tatang's P9.70 'last price,' Tatang amused enough to offer free shoes if CJ brought 30 schoolmates -- CJ brought more than 30, got his pair even though 'some of my chums didn't buy anything' -- the founding anecdote that establishes both Tatang's amused generosity and CJ's lifelong hustle.

The price-detail period color: 'broadsheets and bottled Coke during those bygone days sold for only 10 centavos each. One US dollar exchanged for two pesos' -- using monetary specifics to time-stamp the 1940s.

Sy's Edsa vision recounted 'over sips of tea' at Baron Travel's Makati Arcade office in the 1970s -- describing Edsa then as 'just a four-lane road unpaved in many parts' -- making the supermall prophecy biographically locatable.

Sy's restraint during CJ's 11+ years on the Supreme Court -- 'never spoke with me or intervened in any manner' -- the most institutionally consequential single behavior in the entire portrait, demonstrating that a personal friend of the chief justice can also be a friend of judicial integrity.
Tatang's quiet visit to CJ's retirement reception -- 'showed up, quietly greeted me and left as unobtrusively as when he came in' -- the most poetic single behavioral detail in the column.

Comparison of SM's 5.6 million sqm leasable area to 'the six posh Makati villages (Forbes Park, Dasmariñas, Urdaneta, San Lorenzo, Bel-Air and Magallanes) combined' -- using a uniquely Makati measurement to physicalize SM's scale.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers a personal tribute to Henry Sy Sr. ('Tatang'), tracing their 70-year acquaintance from 1940s Carriedo -- where Sy ran the Park Avenue Shoe Store and CJ was an impoverished grade-school newsboy and shoe-shiner who haggled P9.70 shoes down to free pairs by bringing 30 schoolmates -- to the Sy retail empire of supermalls, BDO bank, and global presence. He recalls Sy's prescient 1970s vision (delivered 'over sips of tea' at the Makati Arcade) that the then-unpaved Edsa would become the metropolitan artery for air-conditioned shopping malls, a prophecy fulfilled through SM City North Edsa, SM Megamall, and SM Mall of Asia -- and now extended via SM Prime's 9.3-million-sqm global footprint, whose leasable 5.6-million sqm exceeds the combined area of the six posh Makati villages. He stresses Sy's defining humility: his self-description of his six children as 'teammates' and Molly as his 'lifetime companion, treasurer, adviser and best friend'; his refusal to speak with or intervene in CJ's affairs during the latter's 11+ years on the Supreme Court out of respect for judicial independence; and his quiet, unobtrusive appearance at CJ's retirement reception. He closes on Sy's philanthropic succession -- the SM Foundation he tended 'as passionately as he did his gigantic businesses' and his deathbed directive to son Hans to expand the Sy-owned National University into 20 campuses with 100,000 scholars -- and prays Tatang's soul rest in peace.
